items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: Louie and I work opposite. And don't think, cause Louie and I was across the street.

ctx.x: Well, there's a couple other fellas here on the list. Joe Oliver, can you tell us what kind of a fella he was?

Fine fella. Swell guy. Full of fun. I work right opposite. Louie and I work opposite. And don't think, cause Louie and I was across the street. Joe Oliver had Bob Schauffer. And he also had Kid Ory. He had Joyce Field there, too. He had Kid Ory with him. Don't think the plantation was packed. Like our place was packed. Both in cabaret right opposite each other. It was packed. Danny had the apex across the street after hours. All the places would be packed. It was a good day. Yeah, it was a good day. Bob Schauffer…
Same Bob Schauffer. Now, Joe was full of fun. Full of fun.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: He said, it's Louie. We know, Cush. I said, you know what I know? You better give up that horn.

ctx.x: Mr. Dominant, really, it seems like you're about to last at the Ohegan's, aren't you? Huh? You're about to last at the Ohegan's, aren't you? Yeah. Me and Louie and I? Yeah. I found on TV the other night. Yeah. He's failing, kid. Yeah, he is.

You know, he called up to it. One time, when he came in, he was at the airport, he called up, he called me. He said, Greg, what'd you know? I said, who's this? He said, it's Louie. We know, Cush. I said, you know what I know? You better give up that horn. I ain't give up that horn, I'm tired of it, man. That's his words, you know. I said, go and die, kill yourself.
I said, Louie, you're not to Louie. You're not young anymore. And that's true. When you get old, Johnny, listen. You cannot. Do the same thing, can you? No, you cannot.
